claims.claim_text: The indexed Seymour J Pomrenze is strongly identified as Sholom (Seymour) Jacob Pomrenze, the archivist whose official biography documents Army and OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The distinctive full name, archivist biography, Army chronology, and explicit OSS service agree with the indexed captain.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence distinctive-name and rank-consistent match with explicit OSS service in an official NARA biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official chronology dates his civilian jobs, Army entry, and 1944-1945 OSS service.
claims.match_notes: Sholom Jacob Pomrenze is recorded as a documented full-name variant.

claims.claim_text: Seymour Pomrenze supervised the Works Progress Administration historic records survey in Chicago during 1940-1941.
claims.evidence_excerpt: supervisor of the Works Progress Administration historic records survey
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official biography dates the Chicago survey role before his National Archives employment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity through the distinctive name and explicit OSS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar government assignment, but not immediate because National Archives and Army service intervened.
claims.match_notes: The specific Chicago survey project is retained rather than collapsed into an undifferentiated WPA entry.

claims.claim_text: The National Archives was Seymour Pomrenze's last documented civilian employer before he joined the United States Army.

claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity through the distinctive name and explicit OSS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit last civilian employment before military service; it is not mislabeled as the immediate OSS predecessor.
claims.match_notes: Army service is separately modeled as the immediate pre-OSS affiliation.

claims.claim_text: Seymour Pomrenze's immediate documented pre-OSS status was service in the United States Army.

claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity through the distinctive name and explicit OSS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit sequence from Army service into OSS service; the source does not identify a narrower Army unit.
claims.match_notes: This is a military assignment, not a civilian employer.
